subject: Post-demo: Queryflow & integration clarifications (SDK, auth, routing, schema)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
To: Ryan Lopez <ryan@logicore.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Queryflow & integration clarifications (SDK, auth, routing, schema)

Hi Ryan — great to meet earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so our eng team can draft a minimal integration plan: 

1) Tech footprint and SDKs
- You mentioned Node for the backend and a small Python microservice for analytics. Can you confirm which service will call the inference API directly? We usually provide Node and Python quickstarts; attaching integration_quickstart.zip.

2) Auth & security
- Do you need API key-based access or do you require OAuth/JWT/KMS integration? Your security lead asked about token rotation and audit logs — we can surface those in the Private/Dedicated options if needed.

3) Routing & fallback
- We'll propose a routing policy: prefer the cost-optimized model for embeddings/reranking, fall back to higher-capacity model for low-latency chat. Any hard constraints (regional routing, data residency)?

4) Structured output, tool-calling, and streaming semantics
- Important: we need to know whether you'll parse partial streaming output (i.e., do you need partial JSON fields as the model streams), or would you rather use function/tool-calling to avoid partial-JSON parsing?
- Also confirm whether your client can handle SSE/websocket-style streaming versus polling.

5) Embeddings & reranking
- Rough QPS for similarity queries and desired candidate set size for rerank (e.g., top-50 -> re-rank). Any constraints on vector store choice or retention?

6) Request/response schema questions
- For the schema we discussed: do you want a single JSON payload (completion-style) or chat-style messages with role tokens? That affects tokenization, max_tokens budgeting, and stop-token semantics.

Action items from our side: Ben/Marissa will draft a 1-page integration pattern with sample request/response and auth options; I want your answers to the above so we can tailor it. Can we target EOD Thursday for a draft and a follow-up call Friday?

Thanks — KM
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachments: integration_quickstart.zip (node/python quickstarts, sample env), mvp_flow.drawio

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Queryflow & integration clarifications (SDK, auth, routing, schema)

Kimberly,

Thanks — good recap. Quick answers below: 

1) SDK & services
- Primary caller will be our Node service (api.logicore). Python svc is for analytics (offline). Node should be the focus.

2) Auth
- We prefer API key initially (rotated weekly by our infra tooling). Longer term we may need OAuth/JWT for third-party access. Security asked for SOC2 + audit logs (can share contact).

3) Routing
- US-only for now. Fallback to a higher-latency model is fine. Ensure model selection can be pinned per environment.

4) Streaming / tool-calling
- Prefer function/tool-calling to avoid streaming partial JSON whenever possible. But if streaming is supported, we can consume SSE partial text; we cannot guarantee robust reassembly of partial, nested JSON in the client.

5) Embeddings & rerank
- Expected peak: ~80 qps similarity queries, candidate set ~200 for final rerank. We plan to use Pinecone but can adapt. Retention: 18 months.

6) Schema preference
- We want explicit structured output: top-level JSON with fields {answer, citations[], source_ids[], score}. Chat-style multi-turn is only for product workflows; many queries are one-shot.

We can do EOD Thursday for the draft and Friday for a 30m follow-up. Also attach the security contact: priya@logicore.io for SOC2.

— Ryan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Queryflow & integration clarifications (SDK, auth, routing, schema)

Ryan — thanks for the quick answers. Below are concrete recommendations and a minimal sample to unblock you. I'm pasting the key pieces; attaching response_schema_examples.json with full examples.

--- SDK init (Node) ---
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RD_API_KEY, region: 'us' });

// If you later move to JWT/OAuth we support token exchange via our token endpoints.

--- Routing / fallback ---
- Use a routing policy: primary=model-a (cost-lean) -> fallback=model-b (latency-safe). Pin per environment via config.
- Ensure your client handles 409/429 with exponential backoff.

--- Chat vs Completions (request/response) ---
- One-shot Qs: completions-like single-input request is simplest and minimizes token overhead.
- Multi-turn workflows: chat messages (role/timestamp) and maintain local KV cache for context; use our streaming or non-streaming chat endpoints depending on UX.

--- Tokenization / max_tokens budgeting ---
- Tokenization differs by model family. Don't assume characters == tokens. We recommend sending a short preflight token-count request for sample inputs if you have strict budgets.
- Two important knobs: max_tokens_out (what you allow model to return) and max_total_tokens (input + output combined). For safety set max_total_tokens = context_window - 32.
- Use stop tokens to delimit the structured JSON. Example stop: ['
---END-STRUCTURE---'] or prefer function-calling to avoid needing to parse partial streams.

--- Streaming semantics ---
- Streaming will emit partial text chunks. If you need to parse structured JSON, streaming can emit invalid intermediate JSON; to avoid, either:
  • use function/tool-calling (structured fields arrive as atomic events), or
  • stream only plain text and post-process after final chunk.

--- Embeddings & Rerank ---
- For QPS/~80 and candidate set 200 we recommend batching vector lookups and running a lightweight approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) + rerank using model-scored relevance.
- Consider caching top-k vectors at application layer for hot queries.

Next steps (from our side):
- Attached response_schema_examples.json: includes (A) completions JSON example, (B) chat messages JSON, (C) function-calling example with tool metadata.
- We'll include suggested stop-token patterns and an SSE example for streaming.

Let us know if you prefer a Node sample that includes streaming reassembly — I can send a small helper library to do chunked reassembly with boundary markers.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
